raw_case_text:
The patient is a 48 years-old female with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented with a 2-day history of right sided flank pain. She described the pain as sudden in onset, radiating to the right but without any other associated symptoms. Review of systems was not significant for any other symptoms. Social history was not significant for any toxic habits. Family history did not reveal any specific information. Vitals revealed heart rate 127 beats/minute, blood pressure of 153/100 mm Hg, respiratory rate 20/minute, temperature of 98.1 degrees F, and oxygen saturation of 100% on room air. Physical examination was significant for right sided abdominal tenderness. Lab investigations were significant for leukocytosis (WBC: 24.0 k/muL [reference range: 4.8-10.8 k/muL], neutrophil percent: 83.0% [reference range: 40.0-70.0%]), anemia (hemoglobin:10.0 g/dl [reference range: 12-16 g/dl]), thrombocytosis (platelets 763k/muL [reference range: 150-400k/muL]) and transaminitis. Urinalysis revealed leukocyte esterase and bacteria suspicious for urinary tract infection. CT scan of abdomen and pelvis without contrast revealed a large 5.6 x 7.9 x 8.4 cm multiloculated collection arising from the lower pole of the right kidney invading the right psoas muscle and a large 8.4 cm multiloculated collection arising from the lower pole of the right kidney as shown in Fig. 1a.
She was empirically started on vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Blood and urine cultures were sent before antibiotic administration. Urology recommended drainage of the lesion that was performed by interventional radiology and a drain was left for further drain output as shown in Fig. 1b.
Her urine cultures were significant for C. koseri. Blood cultures did not reveal any growth. Cultures from abscess drainage were significant for C. koseri, as well. Mycobacterial cultures, PCR for tuberculosis and other microbiological workup was negative. Her antibiotics were de-escalated to ampicillin-sulbactam based on susceptibility report. Repeated imaging revealed mild right hydronephrosis and hydroureter, no obstructing calculus and a 5.3 cm fluid collection with air bubbles in the right flank as Fig. 2.
The patient's drain was, therefore, repositioned and a Foley catheter was placed for urinary obstruction. Cultures from the repeat drain output revealed Cryptococcus and Candida tropicalis. She was empirically started on fluconazole. Her symptoms began to improve. Repeat cultures were negative. The patient was discharged on 4 weeks of intravenous ceftriaxone 2 g once daily, and oral metronidazole 500 mg every 8 h. She was also started on oral fluconazole 400 mg once daily for a year with close outpatient follow-up with infectious disease clinic. A post discharge CT scan obtained showed a decrease in size of the right kidney fluid collection as shown in Fig. 3.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 48-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus presented with a 2-day history of sudden-onset right-sided flank pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed sudden-onset right-sided flank pain radiating to the right 2 days prior to admission, without fever or other associated systemic or urinary symptoms.
subjective.past_medical_history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; no toxic social habits or significant family history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right-sided flank pain. Negative for other systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: heart rate 127 beats/min, blood pressure 153/100 mmHg, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, temperature 98.1 F, oxygen saturation 100% on room air. Abdominal examination was significant for right-sided abdominal/flank tenderness.
objective.routine_investigations: Leukocytosis (WBC 24.0 k/uL; reference: 4.8-10.8 k/uL) with neutrophilia (83.0%; reference: 40.0-70.0%), anemia (hemoglobin 10.0 g/dL; reference: 12-16 g/dL), thrombocytosis (platelets 763 k/uL; reference: 150-400 k/uL), and transaminitis. Urinalysis was positive for leukocyte esterase and bacteriuria; blood cultures were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a large 5.6 x 7.9 x 8.4 cm multiloculated abscess arising from the lower pole of the right kidney invading the right psoas muscle. Repeat CT after initial IR drainage showed mild right hydronephrosis/hydroureter without calculus and a residual 5.3 cm right flank fluid collection containing air bubbles.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of right renal and psoas abscess co-infected with Citrobacter koseri, Cryptococcus spp., and Candida tropicalis, confirmed by initial urine and percutaneous abscess drainage cultures growing C. koseri and subsequent repeat drain output cultures isolating Cryptococcus and Candida tropicalis; tuberculosis was excluded by negative mycobacterial cultures and PCR. Initially treated with empiric vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam (de-escalated to ampicillin-sulbactam) and interventional radiology percutaneous drainage, followed by drain repositioning, Foley catheterization, and oral fluconazole upon fungal isolation. Discharged on 4 weeks of IV ceftriaxone (2 g daily) and oral metronidazole (500 mg every 8 hours) plus a 1-year course of oral fluconazole (400 mg daily), with post-discharge CT confirming abscess reduction.
